sections.title: Verb + -ing or to-infinitive (similar meaning)
sections.content:
Some verbs can be followed by an -ing form or a to-infinitive with little difference in meaning. These include: attempt, begin, can't bear, cease, continue, hate, intend, like, love, prefer, start.
• I began to learn / learning Chinese when I was at university.
However, we often prefer a to-infinitive if the verb itself is in a continuous form:
• I'm beginning to learn Chinese. (not I'm beginning learning Chinese.)
And after like, love, hate, prefer we use an -ing form when we talk about a hobby or something we enjoy, but we use a to-infinitive when we talk about choices / habits:
• I like bouldering. (hobby) but I like to update my blog twice a week. (habit)

sections.title: Verb + -ing or to-infinitive (different meaning)
sections.content:
Other verbs can be followed by an -ing form or a to-infinitive, but there is a difference in meaning. Consider: dread, forget, go on, mean, regret, remember, stop, try.
• I remembered to lock the door. (I didn't forget)
• I remembered locking the door. (I have a memory of it)
• He stopped to smoke. (He stopped what he was doing in order to smoke)
• He stopped smoking. (He gave up the habit)
• I tried to move the table. (I made an effort but failed)
• I tried moving the table. (I moved it to see if the room looked better)

exercises.question: I'm beginning ___ that it was a mistake to come here.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to think
After continuous 'beginning', use to-infinitive. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.

exercises.sentence: I clearly remember to post the letter because I bought stamps specially.
exercises.correction: I clearly remember posting the letter because I bought stamps specially.
exercises.hint: 'Remember + -ing' = recall a past action. 'Remember + to-infinitive' = don't forget (future task).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: remember posting
'Remember + -ing' means to have a memory of a past action: 'I remember locking the door' = I recall doing it. 'Remember + to-infinitive' means not to forget to do a future task: 'Remember to lock the door' = don't forget to do it. The past context here ('bought stamps specially') confirms the -ing form is needed.

exercises.question: I like ___ the room every morning before I start work.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to clean
Talking about a habit/routine. Repeated or habitual actions use the present simple, not the continuous.

exercises.sentence: She stopped to smoke three years ago after her doctor's warning.
exercises.correction: She stopped smoking three years ago after her doctor's warning.
exercises.hint: 'Stop + -ing' = quit that activity. 'Stop + to-infinitive' = pause in order to do something.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: stopped smoking
'Stop + -ing' = give up or quit the activity: 'stopped smoking' means she no longer smokes. 'Stop + to-infinitive' means pause what you're doing in order to do something else: 'She stopped to smoke' would mean she paused (e.g. walking) in order to have a cigarette — the opposite meaning.

exercises.question: I regret ___ him that he hadn't got the job.
exercises.hint: Regret + to-infinitive is used for bad news/formal statements.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to tell
Regret + to-infinitive is used for bad news/formal statements. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.

exercises.question: I tried ___ (open) the window but it was completely stuck.
exercises.hint: 'Try to do' = attempt (but may fail). 'Try doing' = experiment with as a possible solution.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to open
'Try + to-infinitive' means attempt to do something (possibly without success): 'tried to open' = attempted but found it stuck. 'Try + -ing' means experiment with something as a possible solution: 'Try opening the window' = why not try that approach. Here, the stuck window confirms 'tried to open' (attempted, failed).

exercises.question: After two years in the job, she went on ___ the company's youngest manager.
exercises.hint: Go on + to-infinitive = move to a new action.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to become
Go on + to-infinitive = move to a new action. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.

exercises.question: She went on ___ despite the noise.
exercises.hint: Go on + -ing = continue the same action.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: talking
Go on + -ing = continue the same action. This verb pattern requires a gerund (-ing form) as its object.
